thread:
olivia (sec-eng): quick heads-up — we're changing how services load mTLS keystores across regions. goal: encrypt keystores with our KMS CMK (envelope encryption), emit structured audit events for every keystore read/rotate, and tighten RBAC so only operator roles can do manual rotate. any major blockers?
kevin (infra): sounds good. main asks: 1) do envelope keys per-region or per-service? 2) do we grant KMS decrypt rights to service identities or only to a keystore agent? 3) how do we surface audit events to central ELK?
maria (sre): prefer a regional DEK per region, wrapped by a global CMK — avoids cross-region decrypts during failover. we should have a bounded fallback that uses cached DEK for reads if KMS is temporarily unavailable, with a strict TTL.
lisa (prodsec): critical: key policies must not allow direct decrypt for app service accounts. route decrypt through a short-lived keystore-agent (service account with narrow RBAC). prodsec wants 2-person approval for manual rotates. :lock:
alex (platform): adding some concrete snippets. KMS policy idea (very small):
```json
{
  "Principal": {"AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/keystore-agent"]},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:RequestedRegion": "us-east-1"}}
}
```
kevin (infra): exact RBAC roles I'd propose: `keystore-agent`, `keystore-approver`, `keystore-reader` (read only, via agent). keep apps only as callers to agent. also PR #4123 wires agent sidecar.
devops-bot: Deploy scheduled: `keystore-sidecar` v1.7 -> staging at 2026-03-21T02:00Z. CI: green.
maria (sre): audit event schema proposal (single line JSON event emitted to logs):
```json
{"event":"keystore.access","action":"decrypt","service":"payments","region":"eu-west-1","principal":"role/keystore-agent","result":"success","decryption_kms_key":"arn:aws:kms:...:key/...","ts":"2026-03-21T02:03:12Z","request_id":"req-9a7b"}
```
lisa (prodsec): add `sensitive=false|true` flag for whether the keystore contained cert private key material, and include `rotation_initiator` (manual|auto) and `approval_ids` if manual. this helps audits for compliance.
kevin (infra): vulnerability triage note: if rotation fails with `KMS.InvalidCiphertext` or `AccessDenied`, runbook step 1 — check key policy and grant `keystore-agent` `kms:Decrypt`. step 2 — verify STS role session tagging. step 3 — roll back to cached DEK and trigger paging.
sre-oncall: adding minimal emergency rotate script for runbook (keeps it simple):
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# emergency rotate: call platform API which will generate new cert, wrap with KMS, and update secrets
AUTH_TOKEN="$(cat /run/secrets/ops_token)"
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUTH_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://platform-api.internal/v1/keystore/rotate \
  -d '{"service":"payments","region":"eu-west-1","force":true}'
```
olivia (sec-eng): note — manual rotate requires `keystore-approver` approval in the platform UI; we should enforce via RBAC webhook that rejects rotate requests without two approvals. also need audit retention: 2 years for cert events.
alex (platform): I've opened internal RFC: https://phabricator.redwood/PRF/8782 (contains detailed RBAC webhook patch and schema). adding checklist in PR description for prodsec review.
maria (sre): monitoring: create two alerts: 1) `keystore.decrypt.error.rate` > 1% over 5m -> pager, 2) `keystore.rotate.failures` > 1 in 1h -> page ops and sec.
lisa (prodsec): one more: HSM integration for the CMK — confirm with keyops that CMK is FIPS-backed in prod. if not, escalate to compliance.
kevin (infra): deploy plan: staging test with simulated KMS failure, ensure agent can serve cached DEK for 2m, then prod rollout with gradual canary. will add canary tag.
olivia (sec-eng): thanks all — i'll put together final checklist and PR review items. assigning owners: kevin infra for agent changes, alex platform for RBAC webhook, lisa prodsec for policies, maria for runbook/alerts. will update thread when RFC lands. :white_check_mark:
